header: One panel at a time, behind tabs
lead: Two to eight rich-text panels behind a row of tabs. Without JavaScript, the panels show as a stack of sections with headings.

panels.title: With JavaScript
panels.bodytext: The shared script shows one panel at a time. The arrow keys move between the tabs, Home and End jump to the first and the last, and the whole row is a single stop when you tab through the page.

panels.title: Without JavaScript
panels.bodytext: Every panel is in the page and none starts hidden, so the band becomes a stack of headed sections. It is longer, but every word can still be read, printed, searched and indexed.

panels.title: When to use it
panels.bodytext: For instructions per operating system, one product for two audiences, prices per region, or answers for private and business customers. If readers should work through the panels in order, use an accordion.
